references.text: At the consecration of Aaron and his sons to the priestly service, blood was applied to the lobe of the right ear, the thumb of the right hand, and the big toe of the right foot—the same ritual as in the cleansing of a leper.
Moses performed the same action with blood on the lobe of Aaron's right ear, the thumb of his right hand, and the big toe of his right foot during their priestly consecration.
The same verse describes how the oil is also to be applied to the same places as the blood—the lobe of the right ear, the thumb of the right hand, and the big toe of the right foot.
A parallel passage describing the same ritual for someone who is poor and cannot afford a full offering.
The same procedure with oil on the lobe of the right ear, the thumb, and the big toe in connection with the cleansing ritual for the poor person.
The Epistle to the Hebrews explains the significance of blood in cleansing rituals and how almost everything is cleansed with blood according to the law.
